sections.title: New creation and the holy city

blocks.text: Revelation 21 presents a new heaven and new earth, the holy city New Jerusalem descending from heaven, and God's dwelling with humanity. Death, mourning, crying, and pain are no more. The city is measured, surrounded by gates named for Israel's tribes and foundations named for the apostles, and filled with God's glory. It has no temple or sun because the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are its temple and light; the nations and kings enter, while what is unclean does not.

sections.title: From temple history to direct presence

blocks.text: The supplied chronology traces sanctuary presence from the wilderness tabernacle to Solomon's temple, temple judgment and destruction, restored Second Temple worship, and Jesus' temple-fulfillment claim. Revelation 21 brings that trajectory to a city in which the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are themselves the temple, so the vision's sacred space is defined by direct divine presence rather than a separate temple building.

Ancient temples were understood as places of divine dwelling and royal-cultic order. The supplied context describes Israel's temple symbol through holiness, covenant, sacrifice, priesthood, and presence. Revelation 21 transforms that imagery around God's direct presence: the city is holy, but no separate temple is needed because God and the Lamb fill the role of temple and light.

sections.title: Renewal reaches creation and the nations

blocks.text: The ending presents more than private escape: it joins new heaven and new earth, divine dwelling, the end of death and mourning, healing for the nations, and the arrival of the nations' glory. The vision's renewal is therefore cosmic and communal in its own imagery, extending beyond the city's walls to the nations and the whole created order.

sections.title: City, bride, sanctuary, and renewed Zion

blocks.text: New Jerusalem combines city, bride, sanctuary, Eden, and renewed-Zion imagery, while Revelation repeatedly reworks Israel's Scriptures, especially Daniel, Ezekiel, Isaiah, Exodus, Zechariah, Genesis, and Psalms. These images converge in chapter 21's descending city, river-like life imagery, holiness, and restored relationship between God and humanity.
